name: おもてなしダイニング 福亭 (Omotenashi Dining Fukutei)

claims.text: No information about dedicated fryers or separate prep surfaces. Tempura (wheat batter) is a menu staple, raising shared-fryer cross-contamination risk for celiac diners.
Standard Japanese soy sauce (wheat-containing) is almost certainly used throughout the kitchen; no mention of tamari or GF shoyu substitutes anywhere on the menu or official site.
Fish-centric kitchen; dashi stock (bonito/fish-based) is standard across Japanese cuisine and likely used as a base in most dishes including oden broth, rice dishes, and sauces.

A TripAdvisor reviewer reported that staff successfully modified a preset meal for a celiac guest with a few substitutions, and adapted an oden dish to exclude meat on request—suggesting genuine willingness to accommodate, but no formal allergy protocol is documented.
Hitosara lists food allergy considerations as accepted (食物アレルギー対応可). Advance reservation and explicit communication required.
Halal-certified with a dedicated halal menu (anago hitsumabushi, anago tempura); no pork used in halal dishes; on-site prayer space provided—showing serious dietary-protocol awareness.
Fully non-smoking establishment.
Hitosara lists gluten-free accommodations as available (グルテンフリー対応可).
No information on cross-contamination controls available. A busy counter kitchen serving multiple courses is high-risk for shared surfaces and utensils.
Standard wheat-containing soy sauce is standard in Edomae sushi preparation (nigiri brushing, marinades). No tamari or wheat-free shoyu noted anywhere in available sources.
Entire menu centres on fish and seafood; vegan cross-contact is unavoidable.
No allergy or dietary accommodation information found on any platform. Guests should call the restaurant directly before visiting.

name: オーガニックダイニングvegeta (Organic Dining Vegeta)

claims.text: No information about dedicated fryer or separate preparation areas for gluten-free orders. The kitchen serves both wheat-containing dishes (chicken karaage uses breading, hambagu steak may use breadcrumbs) and the organic vegetable dishes in the same space.
Standard Japanese soy sauce (containing wheat) is almost certainly used in marinades, dressings, and cooked dishes. No tamari or GF shoyu alternative is documented on any source reviewed.
Miso soup is served with lunch sets; dashi base (likely bonito/katsuo) is undisclosed. Meat dishes such as pork kimchi and chicken karaage are cooked in the same kitchen.

One TripAdvisor reviewer from July 2024 described staff as 'lovely and accommodating' for a gluten-free diner and called the food 'well presented', but no specifics about protocols, substitutions, or dedicated handling were given.
All rice uses JAS-certified pesticide-free organic cultivation (milky queen or mixed grain), which is inherently gluten-free. Organic vegetable sides and salads form the core of the menu.
Ingredients are sourced direct from Migita Farm (circular agriculture, Tatsuno City) and vetted organic suppliers — likely lower additive load than conventional restaurants.

name: オーガニックラボ リベルテ (Organic Lab Liberte)

claims.text: No information published on soy sauce type used. Menu includes pasta and likely battered items, indicating standard wheat-containing soy sauce is probable.
Venison is the restaurant's signature ingredient and is present across the main menu; cross-contact with game meat is unavoidable for vegan diners.
Organic vegetable sourcing is a stated commitment; the small 10-seat counter format allows direct conversation with whoever is cooking, potentially enabling custom requests.

name: ラーメンマサマサ (Ramen Masamasa)

claims.text: House-made wheat noodles are produced on-site; wheat flour is in active use throughout service. Cross-contamination for anyone with celiac disease or serious wheat allergy is effectively unavoidable.
The shoyu tare uses conventional wheat-containing soy sauce selected by the owner for its aroma profile. No tamari or gluten-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned.

Chicken oil (鶏油) is used in the shoyu ramen broth, niboshi (dried sardine) is a core aromatic in the niboshi ramen, and braised pork features in the mazesoba. Animal products are present in every menu item with no plant-based alternative available.

The owner's background as a detail-obsessed craftsman and his practice of hand-selecting premium ingredients suggest consistent, careful preparation — though no specific allergy protocol has been documented.

No information available on cross-contamination practices. This is a small cafeteria kitchen serving wheat-heavy dishes including battered akashi-yaki and breaded katsu-meshi — assume shared surfaces and utensils.

Himeji oden is served with ginger-soy sauce as a condiment; standard Japanese soy sauce (koikuchi shoyu) contains wheat. Oden broth itself is also likely seasoned with soy sauce. No tamari or gluten-free soy sauce alternatives are mentioned in any source.
Oden broth is typically made with katsuobushi (bonito flakes) dashi. Somen and nyumen soups will contain fish-based broth. No plant-based broth option mentioned in any source.
No allergy-handling information found in any source. The center is run as a social welfare facility; there is no indication of allergy-aware staff training or menus.
Soft-serve ice cream sold on the 1st floor (plain flavours such as vanilla or sesame) may be suitable for some dietary needs — but ingredients are unconfirmed.

name: 炉端とおでん 呼炉凪来 姫路店 (Robata to Oden Koronagirai Himeji)

claims.text: No dedicated GF preparation area or allergen separation is mentioned. Standard izakaya kitchen handles wheat-containing items (udon, yakitori tare, soy-glazed robata) alongside all dishes.

Standard wheat-containing soy sauce (koikuchi shoyu) is presumed throughout — used in robata glazes (corn butter-soy, yam isobe-yaki), yakitori tare, and oden broth seasoning. No tamari or GF soy sauce alternatives are mentioned.

Oden broth is fish-based (bonito and/or konbu dashi). All vegetable robata items are cooked on the same grill used for meat and fish. No separation of cooking surfaces or utensils for plant-based diners is mentioned.
No allergen handling policy is published on any platform reviewed. Direct contact with the restaurant (079-280-8684) is recommended before visiting with serious dietary restrictions.
Plain sashimi (tuna, salmon, yellowtail, sea urchin) is available and would be naturally wheat-free and gluten-free if served without soy sauce or with tamari requested — confirm with staff.
Several vegetable robata items (whole grilled peppers, grilled corn, young corn) could theoretically be requested without soy glaze — ask staff about preparation method.

name: ローマピッツァと窯焼きイタリアン 姫路バル (Roma Pizza to Kamayaki Italian Himeji Baru)

claims.text: Pizza is the core product and all dough is wheat-based. A stone oven shared across all pizzas means ambient flour and gluten contact is unavoidable. No gluten-free crust option has been found.
Standard Italian bar menu — cheese, meat, and seafood are central to the menu. No vegan-safe section or plant-based alternatives confirmed.
